name: enable_or
summary: A regulator enable that is on when either of two sources is: a latched cell (through a diode) or USB (through a divider), clamped to the cell
note: From simple_earring rev 2 (vendored with the bolt earring: boards/bolt-earring/vendor/simple_earring/scripts/circuit.py, whose comments give the reasons and the corner simulations behind each value). D_OR is two silicon diodes in series. The first passes A (the power latch's output: the cell) to EN, a diode drop lower; the second clamps EN to CLAMP (the cell) plus a diode drop, so EN never rises far above the regulator's input. R_TOP and R_BOT make B (USB VBUS) into EN at half of VBUS, so USB turns the regulator on whatever the latch says; R_BOT also holds EN low when neither is present. Silicon, not Schottky: a Schottky's reverse leakage into R_BOT, hot, put enough volts on EN to switch the board on by itself. The NCP730's EN must stay below VIN + 0.3 V: half of VBUS meets that only while the regulator's input is at least VBUS/2 - 0.3 V.

D_OR.note: Two diodes in series: 1 anode of the first, 3 their midpoint, 2 cathode of the second

CLAMP.note: The cell: EN is clamped a diode drop above it

citations.quote: 1 A1 anode (diode 1) 2 K2 cathode (diode 2) 3 K1, A2 cathode (diode 1) and anode (diode 2)
citations.note: Table 2: A on pin 1, CLAMP on pin 2, EN on the midpoint pin 3. KiCad's BAV99 symbol draws the same series pair (pin 1 anode end, pin 3 midpoint, pin 2 cathode end), though it names its pins K 1, A 2, K 3.
IR max per diode: what the clamp diode leaks from CLAMP into EN and R_BOT with the board off.
The same, hot; through R_BOT's 100 kohm even 1 uA is 0.1 V on EN.
VF max at 1 mA: EN is A less this drop (and is clamped this much above CLAMP).
Why EN is clamped to the cell, and why half of VBUS is only safe while the regulator's input is at least VBUS/2 - 0.3 V.
